title: Price the export in parallel, write it in order

blocks.text: The nightly price export has to be on the shops' servers by six in the morning. Pricing a single SKU takes a lot of CPU, and with one thread doing it the export now runs past seven. The pricing code is safe to call from several threads at once. The writer that appends lines to the export file is not, and the shops' import expects the lines in catalogue order.

Finish `export(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/PriceExport.java`. When you're done, several SKUs are priced at the same time, and the writer receives every line, one at a time, in the order of the catalogue. About three lines in total.
The tests run the export in a pool of four threads and use a pricer that is slow for some SKUs.

cases.says: every SKU of the catalogue gets exactly one line, with its price
the pricing of one SKU overlaps with the pricing of another
the lines reach the writer in catalogue order even when a later SKU is priced first

origin.section: One Pipeline Runs in One Mode: the Last parallel() or sequential() Call Wins

concepts: The last parallel() or sequential() call sets the mode of the whole pipeline, so a parallel step followed by an ordered one-at-a-time step needs forEachOrdered or two pipelines.
